title: Are We Ready For An Agent-Native Memory System?
task: Evaluating LLM agent memory systems from a data management perspective
key_results: No single memory architecture dominates across scenarios; localized maintenance is more cost-efficient than global reorganization; 12 representative systems evaluated across 11 datasets
comments: First systematic study decomposing agent memory into core modules, but findings suggest that architectural effectiveness is highly workload-dependent rather than providing generalizable design principles.

hypotheses.result: False—effectiveness depends heavily on workload-architecture alignment

hypotheses.result: False—localized maintenance is more cost-efficient
